g.text: Figure 6B Use Case Specification — UC-04 to UC-06
1. A10 ConciergeAgent announces pending review items with a
tiered overview (9.1); RCA picks the tier to start from, or
filters, sorts and compares evidence in the queue view.
2. A10 presents each ReviewTask (GEN-11): a Judgment with its
reasoning chain, evidence pointers, counter-argument and the
A7 ReviewAgent independent conclusion; an unattributed task
with the rule result; a failed task with the failure reason;
a scope-limited task with the alternative-procedure record.
On "show evidence" A10 opens the source voucher, standard
3. RCA decides within the decision set allowed for the task type;
A10 builds the ReviewRecord verbatim (decision and structured
payload) and submits it via DecisionSubmit; an empty reason is
refused; A1 Orchestrator checks object version, gate state and
the task type x decision matrix, else re-presents.
4. The decision takes effect: confirm; override (new Judgment
A5 EvidenceAgent or A6 FieldworkAgent); dispute_resolution;
scope_limited; rerun (back to executing with rerunParams);
5. A1 recomputes the procedure status: completed only when all
its ReviewTasks are decided, no dispute is open, no extension
or rerun is pending and the period is covered; changed
misstatement or risk data are checked against Loop 3.
6. A10 records the dwell time from presentation to confirmation;
5% of high-confidence items are presented blind (AI conclusion
hidden, RCA judges first, then compares).
7. On "open the workflow of this one", A10 gives drill-down links:
the Judgment's four-layer context, the procedure and agent
3a. normal, blind and unattributed tasks also allow
evidence_unreliable: Judgments relying on that evidence
4a. Uncorrected misstatements exceed 70% of overall materiality
4b. NOCLAR found, or management refuses to remove a scope
each decided ReviewTask has a ReviewRecord;
Judgment, Misstatement and procedure status updated.
a Loop 3 trigger condition in P2,
e.g. uncorrected misstatements exceed 70% of overall
1. An instance detects the trigger at a safe point and raises the
reassessment flag: instances stop at their next safe point,
A1 Orchestrator stops dispatching, completed Judgments are kept.
2. A4 RiskAssessor reads the new evidence and the current
risk_register and re-reasons with the LLM into a risk change
proposal: affected assertions, new level, basis, affected
3. A4 writes reassessment_request; A1 raises the GATE-R
4. A10 ConciergeAgent presents the proposal; RCA approves.
After a fraud trigger, GEN-16 discussion with governance on
the procedures still needed, recorded as GovernanceCommunication.
5. A1 increments the RiskItem version with reason, time and
approver, marks affected completed procedures needs_review
6. A1 enters P1 assembly and re-assembles the procedure pack
without re-ingesting data; after the new PLN-15 version is
approved, new and needs_review procedures run in P2.
1a. Advisory trigger -> no pause; a prompt goes to the review
queue; RCA may start step 2 manually.
4a. RCA rejects -> A10 records the reason, A1 clears the flag and
P2 resumes where it paused (history state).
new plan version approved, new and needs_review procedures run
all P2 procedures in a disposed state (P3).
1. A8 WorkpaperAgent runs FIN-03 to classify accumulated misstatements
and schedules FIN-08; RCA communicates the misstatements to
management and the system records the response.
2. AwaitingCorrection: adjusting entries arrive via API or the offline
pipeline; A6 FieldworkAgent re-runs GEN-05 on the new entries; A8
runs FIN-09 correction verification (corrected, or partially_corrected
with residualAmount); affected completed procedures -> needs_review.
3. A4 RiskAssessor runs PLN-19 materiality reassessment; A9 QCAgent runs
FIN-04 (rollover and iron curtain), FIN-05, FIN-06 and FIN-12; A6 runs
FIN-15, FIN-16, FIN-13, GEN-18 / FIN-17 and EST-06; A4 runs FIN-19;
4. A1 Orchestrator pauses at the gate; A10 ConciergeAgent presents the
uncorrected misstatement summary, scope-limited items, going concern
evaluation, FIN-19 conclusion and FIN-11 statutory reporting matters;
RCA performs FIN-01 and FIN-02 and confirms the opinion type from
5. RCA performs FIN-14 (written governance communication); A5
EvidenceAgent obtains the FIN-07 representation letter; A9 runs
FIN-18 and FIN-10; RCA makes the pre-signature independence and
6. A10 applies the opinion template and has the LLM draft the report and
management letter, each factual assertion pointing to a Judgment;
RCA annotates and A10 revises (version +1) until none remain.
7. A1 checks the EQR record when eqr_required; RCA performs RPT-09,
RPT-10 and RPT-07 (GovernanceCommunication); A10 issues the s307C
8. A1 pauses at the gate; A10 presents the final report, EQR record,
s307C declaration and pre-signature checklist; RCA performs RPT-01,
approves the report version and signs (report date = signing date);
A8 runs RPT-06 archiving and version lock.
3a. Coverage below 100%, a procedure not disposed, or scope_limited
not approved -> blocked with gaps listed.
5a. Core representations missing or unreliable (FIN-18) -> hard
disclaimer candidate in opinion_route; FIN-18 unreliable or
FIN-10 independence breach -> UC-09 via extend (e).
7a. eqr_required and the EQR record incomplete -> blocked.
report version signed and locked (RPT-06), P4;
UC-07 follows as a state transition.
